description: Ivo Daadler, Harvard University Belfer Center Senior Fellow & former US Ambassador to NATO under the Obama Administration, states that progress between US & Iran doesn’t seem likely in the near future because both sides are asking each other to “take a knee and give in.” He also suggest President Trump is underestimating the leverage Iran has, shares why he believes Steve Witkoff & Jared Kushner are not the right people to have nuclear negotiation talks with Iran, and the latest on Russia & Ukraine. title: In A Game of Chicken: Daadler on US-Iran Talks

description: Josh Lipsky, Vice President & Chair of International Economics at the Atlantic Council, suggests Iran will not be on the agenda when Presidents Trump & Xi meet because Trump wants to “come away with the visit with some deliverables.” Lipsky also talks about the impact China is feeling with the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, and if China comes into talks in a stronger position. Josh Lipsky speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s “Balance of Power.” (Source: Bloomberg)

description: Representative Darrell Issa (R-CA), Vice Chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee and a member of the House Judiciary Committee, backs President Trump's push for a federal gas tax holiday, calling the 18-cent cut "symbolic" but still meaningful for consumers despite previously criticizing a similar proposal under the Biden administration. Issa also says China must be "part of the solution" to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and defends staying the course in the Iran conflict despite rising inflation and gas prices, arguing long-term peace outweighs short-term economic pain. description: Sherry Paul, managing director at Morgan Stanley Private Wealth Management and private wealth advisor, said that the wealth held by women has the potential to reshape the economy and be 'more disruptive than AI.' As part of the 'Women, Money, Power' segment Paul shared that her clients are looking for interdependent, collaborative relationships to build their wealth instead of traditional transactional trading.  (Source: Bloomberg)

description: Anthropic is in early talks with investors to raise at least $30 billion in fresh financing, according to people familiar with the matter, setting the stage for what could be its largest funding round yet. description: The King’s Speech is an unusual way to announce government business. description:
US President Donald Trump said he would prioritize trade discussions during his summit with Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping, and downplayed the amount of attention they would devote to the Iran war.
“We’re going to be talking to President Xi about a lot of things. I would say, more than anything, trade,” Trump told reporters Tuesday at the White House as he departed for the highly anticipated meeting in Beijing.
“We have a lot of things to discuss. I wouldn’t say Iran is one of them, to be honest with you, because we have Iran very much under control,” he added. “We’re either going to make a deal or they’re going to be decimated one way or the other.” He spoke to reporters at the White House.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says Trade Not Iran Will Be Priority in Summit With Xi (Q&A)

description:
Donald Trump is expecting economic deals and a “wild” welcome this week in China. In reality, he’ll arrive facing an emboldened Xi Jinping, just as his own hand is constrained by the conflict in Iran. 
When the US president touches down in Beijing on Wednesday evening for a 36-hour summit, it’ll mark his first overseas trip since waging war in the Middle East. Over talks at the Great Hall of the People and a state dinner, followed by morning tea, the leaders will discuss trade, tariffs and the self-ruled island of Taiwan. Another agenda item, of course, is Iran.  Sara Schuman, Managing Director at Beacon Global Strategies and former Senior Trade Representative for China at the Office of the United States Trade Representative joins Balance of Power to discuss.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Faces Emboldened Xi in China as Iran War Clips US Leverage

description:
Michael McKee, Bloomberg International Economics and Policy Correspondent says we can expect Kevin Warsh to be confirmed to Fed Chair with similar numbers.  - The Senate confirmed Kevin Warsh’s nomination to the Federal Reserve Board of Governors Tuesday, with the chamber expected to confirm him separately as chair later this week.
The 51-45 Senate vote Tuesday grants Warsh a 14—year term on the central bank’s board. The Senate plans a procedural vote shortly to pave the way for a vote on Warsh’s confirmation to succeed Jerome Powell as chairman. 
The confirmation vote on the chairmanship is likely to occur Wednesday. The chair’s term runs for four years. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Warsh Confirmed to Fed Board, Still Awaiting Vote on Chair Post
